# RL training run diagnosis

Review the staged post-training experiment and determine whether it is healthy
or unhealthy. Treat the workspace as a historical snapshot: inspect its source,
effective configuration, launch scripts, data processing, reward logic, logs,
tracked metrics, and frozen evaluation evidence. Do not assume that an unusual
setting or implementation is causal without connecting it to observed behavior.

Use held-out evaluation evidence together with rollout, truncation, runtime,
optimization, and training signals. Training reward alone does not establish
held-out health. A truncated log is not by itself proof of a defect.

Do not launch a full training run, use the network, or modify the historical
snapshot. The dataset, held-out set, model, training-step budget, and evaluation
interval are fixed.

## Deliverable

Write one concise UTF-8 diagnosis to:

```text
$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/agent_answer.md
```

State the verdict, identify the concrete root cause or causes, and explain the
causal chain using specific workspace evidence. Distinguish root causes from
symptoms. Do not propose or implement a fix, and do not write other deliverable
files.

1	#!/bin/bash
2	#
3	# Multi-Turn PPO on Endless Terminals with Qwen3-1.7B, on slime v0.3.2.
4	#
5	# The run has two stages:
6	#
7	#   Stage A -- "the previous training run".  A real PPO rollout (actor + critic)
8	#              starting from the base HF model, which saves a Megatron
9	#              checkpoint for both roles.
10	#
11	#   Stage B -- "the model was reloaded".  The actor genuinely resumes from
12	#              Stage A's Megatron checkpoint (weights *and* optimizer state).
13	#              The critic's backbone is reloaded from the base model.  Stage B
14	#              opens with NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS critic-only rollouts (the
15	#              warmup window) and then trains actor and critic jointly.
16	#
17	# The full slime source tree is bundled in the workspace (slime/) and is the
18	# copy that runs -- this script puts it ahead of the image's install on
19	# PYTHONPATH, so editing slime/ here is what takes effect, with nothing to
20	# install first.
21	#
22	# NOTE ON A SHARED HOST: unlike slime's own example scripts this one never runs
23	# `pkill -9 ray / pkill -9 python / ray stop --force` on entry.  It is meant to
24	# run inside its own container, and it brings up a private Ray head on a
25	# non-default port with a private temp dir.
26	
27	set -euo pipefail
28	
29	WS="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" &>/dev/null && pwd)"
30	
31	# The container runs as root while /workspace is a bind mount owned by whoever
32	# checked the case out, so any .pyc written here lands root-owned in their tree
33	# -- and `importlib` copies the *source* file's mode onto the .pyc, so a 600
34	# source yields a 600 root-owned file that even the owner cannot read, and
35	# `cp -r` of the case fails. Nothing here benefits from a bytecode cache.
36	export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
37	
38	MODEL_DIR="${MODEL_DIR:-${WS}/Qwen3-1.7B}"
39	ET_SRC="${ET_SRC:-${WS}/endless-terminals}"
40	SLIME_HOME="${SLIME_HOME:-${WS}/slime}"
41	OUT_DIR="${OUT_DIR:-${WS}/outputs}"
42	CKPT_ROOT="${CKPT_ROOT:-/ckpt}"
43	
44	# Endless Terminals sandbox knobs; also forwarded into the Ray workers, which
45	# read them at import time in et/rollout.py.
46	#
47	# These must NOT live under /dev/shm: it is mounted noexec in the training
48	# image, and many tasks' verifiers assert os.access(path, os.X_OK), which is
49	# False there even at mode 755.
50	export ET_DATA_ROOT="${ET_DATA_ROOT:-/tmp/et_prompts}"
51	export ET_SCRATCH="${ET_SCRATCH:-/tmp/et_episodes}"
52	export ET_MAX_TURNS="${ET_MAX_TURNS:-6}"
53	export ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS="${ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS:-384}"
54	export ET_CMD_TIMEOUT="${ET_CMD_TIMEOUT:-20}"
55	export ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS="${ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS:-1200}"
56	
57	NUM_GPUS="${NUM_GPUS:-2}"
58	TP_SIZE="${TP_SIZE:-2}"
59	SGLANG_MEM_FRACTION="${SGLANG_MEM_FRACTION:-0.55}"
60	# Rollouts per stage. Both stages use the same count on purpose, and must:
61	# slime derives `train_iters` from `--num-rollout` (model.py:203) and Megatron
62	# stores the resulting LR/weight-decay horizons inside the checkpoint, then
63	# asserts on reload that they match the ones the new arguments imply
64	# ("total number of iterations do not match"). Giving Stage B a different
65	# rollout count than Stage A would trip that assert before any training runs.
66	# In Stage A these rollouts are ordinary PPO; Stage B opens with
67	# NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS critic-only rollouts -- the warmup window -- and then
68	# trains actor and critic jointly for the rest.
69	NUM_ROLLOUTS="${NUM_ROLLOUTS:-2}"
70	# Stage B is the long one: critic warmup followed by joint PPO, trained until
71	# the validation pass rate stops moving. It no longer has to match Stage A's
72	# rollout count -- see --override-opt-param-scheduler at the submit site.
73	NUM_ROLLOUTS_B="${NUM_ROLLOUTS_B:-${NUM_ROLLOUTS}}"
74	# Rollouts at the start of Stage B in which only the critic trains. This is the
75	# warmup window the incident was reported against, and the window in which the
76	# value loss is measured.
77	NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS="${NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS:-${NUM_ROLLOUTS_B}}"
78	
79	# Episodes per rollout = ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE x N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT; optimizer
80	# steps per rollout = that, divided by GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE.
81	ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE="${ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE:-8}"
82	N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT="${N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT:-2}"
83	GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE="${GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE:-8}"
84	LR="${LR:-1e-6}"
85	
86	# How many leading critic optimizer steps the reported warmup statistics cover.
87	# Derived rather than guessed, because once Stage B runs past the critic-only
88	# phase the two are no longer the same thing: averaging the value loss over all
89	# of a 30-rollout Stage B measures mostly a critic that has already been
90	# trained, which is not what "warmup value loss" names and not what the
91	# incident was about.
92	CRITIC_WARMUP_STEPS=$(( NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS * ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE * N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT / GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE ))
93	[ "${CRITIC_WARMUP_STEPS}" -gt 0 ] || CRITIC_WARMUP_STEPS=1
94	
95	# Held-out evaluation during Stage B. 0 disables it, which is what the short
96	# value-loss-only reproduction wants.
97	#
98	# val and test get different sample budgets. val only has to say *when* the
99	# curve flattens, so 2 samples x 150 tasks is enough; test carries the
100	# end-to-end claim and is compared per task, where the useful quantity is each
101	# task's success *rate*, which 1 or 2 samples cannot resolve at all.
102	EVAL_INTERVAL="${EVAL_INTERVAL:-0}"
103	N_EVAL_SAMPLES="${N_EVAL_SAMPLES:-2}"
104	N_EVAL_SAMPLES_TEST="${N_EVAL_SAMPLES_TEST:-4}"
105	
106	# How often Stage B checkpoints. Trained to convergence, Stage B runs for well
107	# over an hour, which on a shared host is long enough to be interrupted -- two
108	# runs of this case were killed from outside the container mid-training, once
109	# with SIGTERM and once with SIGKILL. So Stage B saves as it goes and a second
110	# invocation picks up where the first stopped, instead of starting the hour
111	# again. 0 disables it, which is what the short value-loss-only reproduction
112	# wants: it writes nothing and measures only the reload.
113	STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL="${STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL:-0}"
114	
115	RAY_PORT="${RAY_PORT:-6479}"
116	DASH_PORT="${DASH_PORT:-8277}"
117	RAY_TMP="${RAY_TMP:-/tmp/ray_ppo}"
118	
119	mkdir -p "${OUT_DIR}" "${CKPT_ROOT}" "${ET_SCRATCH}"
120	
121	# --------------------------------------------------------- 0. the slime source
122	# The full slime source tree is bundled in the workspace (${SLIME_HOME}) and is
123	# put ahead of the image's editable install on PYTHONPATH below, so it is the
124	# copy that trains -- there is nothing to install first.
125	test -f "${SLIME_HOME}/train.py" || {
126	    echo "FATAL: bundled slime source not found at ${SLIME_HOME}" >&2
127	    exit 1
128	}
129	
130	# ------------------------------------------------------- 1. the prompt dataset
131	# prepare.sh ships the already-built dataset (transpiled + validated + split) at
132	# ${WS}/et_prompts. Seed ET_DATA_ROOT from it so the build below is skipped: the
133	# 2492->1489 admission is environment-fixed and reproducible, so there is no need
134	# to re-run the ~40min transpile+validate pass (and ET_SRC is never read). The
135	# copy lands in a writable, exec-capable dir (ET_DATA_ROOT defaults to /tmp) --
136	# the bundled tree under /workspace may be a root-owned bind mount. If the
137	# prebuilt payload is absent, fall through to building from ET_SRC as before.
138	if [ ! -s "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals.jsonl" ] && [ -s "${WS}/et_prompts/endless_terminals.jsonl" ]; then
139	    echo "=== seeding ET_DATA_ROOT from prebuilt ${WS}/et_prompts (skipping transpile+validate) ==="
140	    mkdir -p "${ET_DATA_ROOT}"
141	    cp -a "${WS}/et_prompts/." "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/"
142	fi
143	if [ ! -s "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals.jsonl" ]; then
144	    echo "=== transpiling + validating the Endless Terminals tasks ==="
145	    (cd "${WS}" && python3 -m et.build_dataset --src "${ET_SRC}" --out "${ET_DATA_ROOT}") \
146	        2>&1 | tee "${OUT_DIR}/build_dataset.log"
147	fi
148	# Deliberately not silenced. A report that is quietly 0 bytes is worse than one
149	# that is loudly absent: it reads as "every task was rejected" to anyone who
150	# opens it later, and that has happened here more than once.
151	copy_artifact() {   # copy_artifact <src>
152	    local src="$1" dst="${OUT_DIR}/$(basename "$1")"
153	    if ! cp -f "${src}" "${dst}"; then
154	        echo "WARNING: could not copy ${src} into ${OUT_DIR}" >&2
155	    elif [ ! -s "${dst}" ] && [ -s "${src}" ]; then
156	        echo "WARNING: ${dst} came out empty although ${src} is not" >&2
157	    fi
158	}
159	copy_artifact "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/validation_report.json"
160	N_PROMPTS="$(wc -l < "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals.jsonl")"
161	echo "prompt set: ${N_PROMPTS} validated Endless Terminals tasks"
162	if [ "${N_PROMPTS}" -lt 4 ]; then
163	    echo "FATAL: too few tasks survived validation to train on." >&2
164	    exit 1
165	fi
166	
167	# Train on one part of the task set and measure on another. The split is a pure
168	# function of the admitted list and a fixed seed, so every run trains and is
169	# scored on exactly the same tasks -- otherwise a comparison between runs is
170	# partly measuring which tasks each one happened to get.
171	if [ ! -s "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals_train.jsonl" ]; then
172	    (cd "${WS}" && python3 -m et.make_splits --prompts "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals.jsonl")
173	fi
174	copy_artifact "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/splits.json"
175	TRAIN_SPLIT="${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals_train.jsonl"
176	VAL_SPLIT="${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals_val.jsonl"
177	TEST_SPLIT="${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals_test.jsonl"
178	printf 'splits: train %s / val %s / test %s\n' \
179	    "$(wc -l < "${TRAIN_SPLIT}")" "$(wc -l < "${VAL_SPLIT}")" "$(wc -l < "${TEST_SPLIT}")"
180	
181	# ------------------------------------------------------------- 2. shared args
182	source "${WS}/configs/model_args.sh"
183	
184	ROLLOUT_ARGS=(
185	    --prompt-data "${TRAIN_SPLIT}"
186	    --input-key prompt
187	    --label-key label
188	    --rollout-shuffle
189	    --rollout-batch-size "${ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE}"
190	    --n-samples-per-prompt "${N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT}"
191	    --rollout-max-response-len 2048
192	    --rollout-temperature 1.0
193	    --global-batch-size "${GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE}"
194	    --balance-data
195	    # The multi-turn terminal loop and its pytest-based episode reward.
196	    --custom-generate-function-path et.rollout.generate
197	    --custom-rm-path et.rollout.reward_func
198	)
199	
200	PPO_ARGS=(
201	    --advantage-estimator ppo   # -> args.use_critic
202	    --gamma 1.0
203	    --lambd 1.0
204	    --eps-clip 0.2
205	    --value-clip 0.2
206	    --kl-coef 0.0               # no reference model, hence no --ref-load and
207	    --entropy-coef 0.0          # no HF -> torch_dist conversion step
208	)
209	
210	PERF_ARGS=(
211	    --tensor-model-parallel-size "${TP_SIZE}"
212	    --pipeline-model-parallel-size 1
213	    --context-parallel-size 1
214	    --recompute-granularity full
215	    --recompute-method uniform
216	    --recompute-num-layers 1
217	    --use-dynamic-batch-size
218	    --max-tokens-per-gpu 8192
219	)
220	# Sequence parallelism splits the activations of the non-tensor-parallel ops
221	# across the TP group, so it is only defined for TP > 1; Megatron asserts on it.
222	# Spelled as an `if` rather than `[ ... ] && ...`: the latter evaluates to the
223	# test's status, which under `set -e` ends the script whenever TP_SIZE is 1.
224	if [ "${TP_SIZE}" -gt 1 ]; then
225	    PERF_ARGS+=(--sequence-parallel)
226	fi
227	
228	OPTIMIZER_ARGS=(
229	    --optimizer adam
230	    --lr "${LR}"
231	    --lr-decay-style constant
232	    --weight-decay 0.0
233	    --adam-beta1 0.9
234	    --adam-beta2 0.95
235	)
236	
237	SGLANG_ARGS=(
238	    --rollout-num-gpus-per-engine "${NUM_GPUS}"
239	    # Colocated: this fraction is what SGLang keeps, and Megatron's weights,
240	    # gradients and Adam state have to fit in the rest. At TP 2 each GPU carries
241	    # half of each role, so 0.55 leaves enough; drop it when NUM_GPUS is 1 and
242	    # one device has to hold both roles whole.
243	    --sglang-mem-fraction-static "${SGLANG_MEM_FRACTION}"
244	)
245	
246	# Held-out scoring, used only by Stage B. slime evaluates once before the first
247	# rollout and then every EVAL_INTERVAL rollouts, which gives both the starting
248	# pass rate and the curve that says whether training has converged.
249	#
250	# val and test are evaluated at the same points on purpose. The convergence
251	# *decision* is read off val; test is reported only at the final point, and
252	# evaluating it throughout costs generation but no statistical validity, since
253	# nothing about the run is conditioned on it.
254	#
255	# Spelled as an --eval-config YAML rather than --eval-prompt-data because the
256	# two splits need different sample counts, and --n-samples-per-eval-prompt is
257	# one global number. Everything the YAML leaves out still falls back to the
258	# command line (eval_config.py:10 DATASET_RUNTIME_SPECS), so temperature,
259	# response length and the prompt/label keys are set once, below and above.
260	EVAL_ARGS=()
261	if [ "${EVAL_INTERVAL}" -gt 0 ]; then
262	    cat > "${OUT_DIR}/eval_datasets.yaml" <<YAML
263	eval:
264	  datasets:
265	    - name: et_val
266	      path: ${VAL_SPLIT}
267	      n_samples_per_eval_prompt: ${N_EVAL_SAMPLES}
268	    - name: et_test
269	      path: ${TEST_SPLIT}
270	      n_samples_per_eval_prompt: ${N_EVAL_SAMPLES_TEST}
271	YAML
272	    EVAL_ARGS=(
273	        --eval-interval "${EVAL_INTERVAL}"
274	        --eval-config "${OUT_DIR}/eval_datasets.yaml"
275	        --eval-max-response-len 2048
276	        --eval-temperature 1.0
277	        --log-passrate
278	        --custom-eval-rollout-log-function-path et.eval_log.log_eval_rollout_data
279	    )
280	fi
281	
282	MISC_ARGS=(
283	    --attention-dropout 0.0
284	    --hidden-dropout 0.0
285	    --accumulate-allreduce-grads-in-fp32
286	    --attention-softmax-in-fp32
287	    --attention-backend flash
288	    --seed 1234
289	)
290	
291	# --------------------------------------------------------- 3. per-role configs
292	# Actor and critic share `args.save` by default, which would make them clobber
293	# each other's checkpoints (the critic's output layer is [1, hidden_size], the
294	# actor's is [vocab, hidden_size]), so each role gets its own directory.
295	cat > "${OUT_DIR}/megatron_roles_stage_a.yaml" <<YAML
296	# Stage A: "the previous training run". Both roles start from the base model.
297	megatron:
298	  - name: stage-a-actor
299	    role: actor
300	    overrides:
301	      load: ${MODEL_DIR}
302	      save: ${CKPT_ROOT}/actor
303	  - name: stage-a-critic
304	    role: critic
305	    overrides:
306	      load: ${MODEL_DIR}
307	      save: ${CKPT_ROOT}/critic
308	YAML
309	
310	# Stage B can be entered two ways, and they are not the same event.
311	#
312	#   fresh   -- "the model was reloaded". The actor resumes from Stage A's
313	#              Megatron checkpoint; the critic's backbone comes from the base
314	#              model.
315	#
316	#   resume  -- an interrupted Stage B being continued. Both roles load Stage B's
317	#              own checkpoints, optimizer state included, and the run continues
318	#              from the last saved rollout. The first attempt's log is kept,
319	#              not overwritten (see the STAGE_B_LOG choice below).
320	STAGE_B_RESUME=0
321	if [ -f "${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_actor/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt" ] \
322	   && [ -f "${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_critic/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt" ]; then
323	    STAGE_B_RESUME=1
324	fi
325	
326	if [ "${STAGE_B_RESUME}" = "1" ]; then
327	    STAGE_B_ACTOR_LOAD="${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_actor"
328	    STAGE_B_CRITIC_LOAD="${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_critic"
329	else
330	    STAGE_B_ACTOR_LOAD="${CKPT_ROOT}/actor"
331	    STAGE_B_CRITIC_LOAD="${MODEL_DIR}"
332	fi
333	
334	cat > "${OUT_DIR}/megatron_roles_stage_b.yaml" <<YAML
335	# Stage B, $([ "${STAGE_B_RESUME}" = "1" ] && echo "resumed from its own checkpoints" || echo "entered fresh after a reload").
336	megatron:

Everything the YAML leaves out still falls back to the\n# command line (eval_config.py:10 DATASET_RUNTIME_SPECS), so temperature,\n# response length and the prompt/label keys are set once, below and above.\nEVAL_ARGS=()\nif [ \"${EVAL_INTERVAL}\" -gt 0 ]; then\n    cat > \"${OUT_DIR}/eval_datasets.yaml\" <<YAML\neval:\n  datasets:\n    - name: et_val\n      path: ${VAL_SPLIT}\n      n_samples_per_eval_prompt: ${N_EVAL_SAMPLES}\n    - name: et_test\n      path: ${TEST_SPLIT}\n      n_samples_per_eval_prompt: ${N_EVAL_SAMPLES_TEST}\nYAML\n    EVAL_ARGS=(\n        --eval-interval \"${EVAL_INTERVAL}\"\n        --eval-config \"${OUT_DIR}/eval_datasets.yaml\"\n        --eval-max-response-len 2048\n        --eval-temperature 1.0\n        --log-passrate\n        --custom-eval-rollout-log-function-path et.eval_log.log_eval_rollout_data\n    )\nfi\n\nMISC_ARGS=(\n    --attention-dropout 0.0\n    --hidden-dropout 0.0\n    --accumulate-allreduce-grads-in-fp32\n    --attention-softmax-in-fp32\n    --attention-backend flash\n    --seed 1234\n)\n\n# --------------------------------------------------------- 3. per-role configs\n# Actor and critic share `args.save` by default, which would make them clobber\n# each other's checkpoints (the critic's output layer is [1, hidden_size], the\n# actor's is [vocab, hidden_size]), so each role gets its own directory.\ncat > \"${OUT_DIR}/megatron_roles_stage_a.yaml\" <<YAML\n# Stage A: \"the previous training run\". Both roles start from the base model.\nmegatron:\n  - name: stage-a-actor\n    role: actor\n    overrides:\n      load: ${MODEL_DIR}\n      save: ${CKPT_ROOT}/actor\n  - name: stage-a-critic\n    role: critic\n    overrides:\n      load: ${MODEL_DIR}\n      save: ${CKPT_ROOT}/critic\nYAML\n\n# Stage B can be entered two ways, and they are not the same event.\n#\n#   fresh   -- \"the model was reloaded\". The actor resumes from Stage A's\n#              Megatron checkpoint; the critic's backbone comes from the base\n#              model.\n#\n#   resume  -- an interrupted Stage B being continued. Both roles load Stage B's\n#              own checkpoints, optimizer state included, and the run continues\n#              from the last saved rollout. The first attempt's log is kept,\n#              not overwritten (see the STAGE_B_LOG choice below).\nSTAGE_B_RESUME=0\nif [ -f \"${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_actor/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt\" ] \\\n   && [ -f \"${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_critic/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt\" ]; then\n    STAGE_B_RESUME=1\nfi\n\nif [ \"${STAGE_B_RESUME}\" = \"1\" ]; then\n    STAGE_B_ACTOR_LOAD=\"${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_actor\"\n    STAGE_B_CRITIC_LOAD=\"${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_critic\"\nelse\n    STAGE_B_ACTOR_LOAD=\"${CKPT_ROOT}/actor\"\n    STAGE_B_CRITIC_LOAD=\"${MODEL_DIR}\"\nfi\n\ncat > \"${OUT_DIR}/megatron_roles_stage_b.yaml\" <<YAML\n# Stage B, $([ \"${STAGE_B_RESUME}\" = \"1\" ] && echo \"resumed from its own checkpoints\" || echo \"entered fresh after a reload\").\nmegatron:\n  - name: stage-b-actor\n    role: actor\n    overrides:\n      load: ${STAGE_B_ACTOR_LOAD}\n      save: ${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_actor\n  - name: stage-b-critic\n    role: critic\n    overrides:\n      load: ${STAGE_B_CRITIC_LOAD}\n      save: ${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_critic\nYAML\n\n# ------------------------------------------------------------------- 4. ray\nexport PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1\n\nray start --head \\\n    --node-ip-address 127.0.0.1 \\\n    --port \"${RAY_PORT}\" \\\n    --num-gpus \"${NUM_GPUS}\" \\\n    --disable-usage-stats \\\n    --dashboard-host 127.0.0.1 \\\n    --dashboard-port \"${DASH_PORT}\" \\\n    --temp-dir \"${RAY_TMP}\"\ntrap 'ray stop --force >/dev/null 2>&1 || true' EXIT\n\n# `|| true` on the whole pipeline, not decoration: under `pipefail` a `grep`\n# that matches nothing fails the pipeline, so on a host with no NVLink -- or in\n# a container holding a single GPU, where the topology matrix has no peer links\n# to report -- `set -e` would kill the script here. Silently: this sits between\n# `ray start` and the first echo of Stage A, so the log just stops.\nNVLINK_COUNT=\"$(nvidia-smi topo -m 2>/dev/null | grep -o 'NV[0-9][0-9]*' | wc -l || true)\"\nHAS_NVLINK=0\n[ \"${NVLINK_COUNT:-0}\" -gt 0 ] && HAS_NVLINK=1\n\nRUNTIME_ENV_JSON=\"{\n  \\\"env_vars\\\": {\n    \\\"PYTHONPATH\\\": \\\"/root/Megatron-LM/:${SLIME_HOME}:${WS}\\\",\n    \\\"CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS\\\": \\\"1\\\",\n    \\\"NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE\\\": \\\"${HAS_NVLINK}\\\",\n    \\\"ET_DATA_ROOT\\\": \\\"${ET_DATA_ROOT}\\\",\n    \\\"ET_EVAL_DUMP_DIR\\\": \\\"${OUT_DIR}/eval_episodes\\\",\n    \\\"ET_SCRATCH\\\": \\\"${ET_SCRATCH}\\\",\n    \\\"ET_MAX_TURNS\\\": \\\"${ET_MAX_TURNS}\\\",\n    \\\"ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS\\\": \\\"${ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS}\\\",\n    \\\"ET_CMD_TIMEOUT\\\": \\\"${ET_CMD_TIMEOUT}\\\",\n    \\\"ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS\\\": \\\"${ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS}\\\"\n  }\n}\"\n\nsubmit() {   # submit <log-file> <extra args...>\n    local log=\"$1\"; shift\n    # The entrypoint is an absolute path on purpose: `ray job submit` does not\n    # run it in this shell's directory but in the cwd of the Ray head (here\n    # /workspace, since no `working_dir` is uploaded), so a bare `train.py`\n    # would not be found. Running ${SLIME_HOME}/train.py puts the bundled slime\n    # tree on the driver's sys.path[0]; the ray workers get it from ${SLIME_HOME}\n    # on PYTHONPATH (RUNTIME_ENV_JSON above), ahead of the image's install.\n    ray job submit \\\n        --address \"http://127.0.0.1:${DASH_PORT}\" \\\n        --runtime-env-json \"${RUNTIME_ENV_JSON}\" \\\n        -- python3 \"${SLIME_HOME}/train.py\" \\\n        --actor-num-nodes 1 \\\n        --actor-num-gpus-per-node \"${NUM_GPUS}\" \\\n        --colocate \\\n        --hf-checkpoint \"${MODEL_DIR}\" \\\n        \"${MODEL_ARGS[@]}\" \\\n        \"${ROLLOUT_ARGS[@]}\" \\\n        \"${PPO_ARGS[@]}\" \\\n        \"${PERF_ARGS[@]}\" \\\n        \"${OPTIMIZER_ARGS[@]}\" \\\n        \"${SGLANG_ARGS[@]}\" \\\n        \"${MISC_ARGS[@]}\" \\\n        \"$@\" 2>&1 | tee \"${log}\"\n}\n\n# Ray forwards actor stdout to the job driver, but keep the raw worker logs too:\n# the per-step metrics are emitted by the train actors, not by the driver.\ncollect_worker_logs() {   # collect_worker_logs <tag>\n    # Two statements, not one: `local a=.. b=..` expands every word before it\n    # assigns any of them, so referring to ${tag} on the same line would read\n    # it while it is still unset -- fatal under `set -u`.\n    local tag=\"$1\"\n    local dst=\"${OUT_DIR}/${tag}_worker_logs\"\n    mkdir -p \"${dst}\"\n    grep -rl \"critic-step\" \"${RAY_TMP}\"/session_*/logs/ 2>/dev/null | while read -r f; do\n        cp -f \"${f}\" \"${dst}/$(basename \"$(dirname \"${f}\")\")_$(basename \"${f}\")\" 2>/dev/null || true\n    done\n}\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 5. stage A\necho\necho \"############ Stage A: the previous training run ############\"\n# SKIP_STAGE_A=1 reuses a checkpoint an earlier invocation already wrote, for\n# re-running the long Stage B after an interruption. Off by default, and\n# refuses to be silently wrong: with no checkpoint there, Stage A runs anyway.\nif [ \"${SKIP_STAGE_A:-0}\" = \"1\" ] && [ -f \"${CKPT_ROOT}/actor/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt\" ]; then\n    echo \"SKIP_STAGE_A=1 and ${CKPT_ROOT}/actor already holds a checkpoint -- reusing it.\"\nelse\n    submit \"${OUT_DIR}/stage_a.log\" \\\n        --megatron-config-path \"${OUT_DIR}/megatron_roles_stage_a.yaml\" \\\n        --load \"${MODEL_DIR}\" \\\n        --save \"${CKPT_ROOT}/actor\" \\\n        --save-interval 1 \\\n        --num-rollout \"${NUM_ROLLOUTS}\" \\\n        --num-critic-only-steps 0\n    collect_worker_logs stage_a\nfi\n\necho\necho \"checkpoint written by Stage A:\"\nls -1 \"${CKPT_ROOT}/actor\" 2>/dev/null || true\ntest -f \"${CKPT_ROOT}/actor/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt\" || {\n    echo \"FATAL: Stage A did not produce a resumable Megatron checkpoint.\" >&2\n    exit 1\n}\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 6. stage B\necho\necho \"############ Stage B: reload, then critic warmup ############\"\n# --save-interval has to be set because --save is: Megatron's validate_args\n# asserts the two go together. With STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL=0 it is set far\n# larger than the number of rollouts Stage B takes, so Stage B measures the\n# reload and writes nothing -- the only checkpoint the short reproduction needs\n# is the one Stage A already produced.\n#\n# --override-opt-param-scheduler is what lets Stage B be longer than Stage A.\n# slime derives `train_iters` from --num-rollout (model.py:203) and Megatron\n# stores the resulting LR/weight-decay horizons in the checkpoint, then asserts\n# on reload that the new arguments imply the same ones (\"total number of\n# iterations do not match\"). The flag says \"use the command line, not the\n# checkpoint\", which is exactly right here: Stage B is a new training run that\n# happens to start from Stage A's weights, not a resumption of Stage A.\nSTAGE_B_ARGS=(\n    --megatron-config-path \"${OUT_DIR}/megatron_roles_stage_b.yaml\"\n    --load \"${STAGE_B_ACTOR_LOAD}\"\n    --save \"${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_actor\"\n    --save-interval \"$([ \"${STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL}\" -gt 0 ] && echo \"${STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL}\" || echo 1000)\"\n    --override-opt-param-scheduler\n    --num-rollout \"${NUM_ROLLOUTS_B}\"\n    --num-critic-only-steps \"${NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS}\"\n)\n\nSTAGE_B_LOG=\"${OUT_DIR}/stage_b.log\"\nif [ \"${STAGE_B_RESUME}\" = \"1\" ]; then\n    # The first attempt's log holds the warmup window that the value-loss\n    # verdict is read from, so a resume must not overwrite it.\n    n=1\n    while [ -e \"${OUT_DIR}/stage_b_resume_${n}.log\" ]; do n=$((n + 1)); done\n    STAGE_B_LOG=\"${OUT_DIR}/stage_b_resume_${n}.log\"\n    echo \"resuming Stage B from ${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_{actor,critic}\" \\\n         \"(iteration $(cat \"${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_critic/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt\")); log -> ${STAGE_B_LOG}\"\n    # --start-rollout-id is deliberately NOT passed here. slime takes the start\n    # id from the *critic*'s loaded checkpoint when a critic is in play\n    # (placement_group.py:212), and Stage B saves at `iteration = rollout_id`,\n    # so omitting it resumes at exactly the rollout after the last saved one.\nelse\n    # --start-rollout-id 0 pins the warmup window: without it the start id is\n    # inferred from whichever checkpoint the critic loaded, and on a fresh\n    # Stage B the critic loads a plain HF directory (iteration 0).\n    STAGE_B_ARGS+=(--start-rollout-id 0)\nfi\n\nsubmit \"${STAGE_B_LOG}\" \"${STAGE_B_ARGS[@]}\" \"${EVAL_ARGS[@]+\"${EVAL_ARGS[@]}\"}\"\ncollect_worker_logs stage_b\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 7. verdict\necho\necho \"############ critic warmup value loss ############\"\npython3 \"${WS}/tools/parse_value_loss.py\" \\\n    \"${OUT_DIR}/stage_b.log\" \\\n    --warmup-steps \"${CRITIC_WARMUP_STEPS}\" \\\n    --out \"${OUT_DIR}/stage_b_value_loss.json\"\n\npython3 \"${WS}/tools/parse_value_loss.py\" \\\n    \"${OUT_DIR}/stage_a.log\" \\\n    --out \"${OUT_DIR}/stage_a_value_loss.json\" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true\n\necho\necho \"artifacts in ${OUT_DIR}:\"\nls -1 \"${OUT_DIR}\"\n", "numLines": 517, "startLine": 1, "totalLines": 517}}

#!/bin/bash
#
# Multi-Turn PPO on Endless Terminals with Qwen3-1.7B, on slime v0.3.2.
#
# The run has two stages:
#
#   Stage A -- "the previous training run".  A real PPO rollout (actor + critic)
#              starting from the base HF model, which saves a Megatron
#              checkpoint for both roles.
#
#   Stage B -- "the model was reloaded".  The actor genuinely resumes from
#              Stage A's Megatron checkpoint (weights *and* optimizer state).
#              The critic's backbone is reloaded from the base model.  Stage B
#              opens with NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS critic-only rollouts (the
#              warmup window) and then trains actor and critic jointly.
#
# The full slime source tree is bundled in the workspace (slime/) and is the
# copy that runs -- this script puts it ahead of the image's install on
# PYTHONPATH, so editing slime/ here is what takes effect, with nothing to
# install first.
#
# NOTE ON A SHARED HOST: unlike slime's own example scripts this one never runs
# `pkill -9 ray / pkill -9 python / ray stop --force` on entry.  It is meant to
# run inside its own container, and it brings up a private Ray head on a
# non-default port with a private temp dir.

set -euo pipefail

WS="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" &>/dev/null && pwd)"

# The container runs as root while /workspace is a bind mount owned by whoever
# checked the case out, so any .pyc written here lands root-owned in their tree
# -- and `importlib` copies the *source* file's mode onto the .pyc, so a 600
# source yields a 600 root-owned file that even the owner cannot read, and
# `cp -r` of the case fails. Nothing here benefits from a bytecode cache.
export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1

MODEL_DIR="${MODEL_DIR:-${WS}/Qwen3-1.7B}"
ET_SRC="${ET_SRC:-${WS}/endless-terminals}"
SLIME_HOME="${SLIME_HOME:-${WS}/slime}"
OUT_DIR="${OUT_DIR:-${WS}/outputs}"
CKPT_ROOT="${CKPT_ROOT:-/ckpt}"

# Endless Terminals sandbox knobs; also forwarded into the Ray workers, which
# read them at import time in et/rollout.py.
#
# These must NOT live under /dev/shm: it is mounted noexec in the training
# image, and many tasks' verifiers assert os.access(path, os.X_OK), which is
# False there even at mode 755.
export ET_DATA_ROOT="${ET_DATA_ROOT:-/tmp/et_prompts}"
export ET_SCRATCH="${ET_SCRATCH:-/tmp/et_episodes}"
export ET_MAX_TURNS="${ET_MAX_TURNS:-6}"
export ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS="${ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS:-384}"
export ET_CMD_TIMEOUT="${ET_CMD_TIMEOUT:-20}"
export ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS="${ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS:-1200}"

NUM_GPUS="${NUM_GPUS:-2}"
TP_SIZE="${TP_SIZE:-2}"
SGLANG_MEM_FRACTION="${SGLANG_MEM_FRACTION:-0.55}"
# Rollouts per stage. Both stages use the same count on purpose, and must:
# slime derives `train_iters` from `--num-rollout` (model.py:203) and Megatron
# stores the resulting LR/weight-decay horizons inside the checkpoint, then
# asserts on reload that they match the ones the new arguments imply
# ("total number of iterations do not match"). Giving Stage B a different
# rollout count than Stage A would trip that assert before any training runs.
# In Stage A these rollouts are ordinary PPO; Stage B opens with
# NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS critic-only rollouts -- the warmup window -- and then
# trains actor and critic jointly for the rest.
NUM_ROLLOUTS="${NUM_ROLLOUTS:-2}"
# Stage B is the long one: critic warmup followed by joint PPO, trained until
# the validation pass rate stops moving. It no longer has to match Stage A's
# rollout count -- see --override-opt-param-scheduler at the submit site.
NUM_ROLLOUTS_B="${NUM_ROLLOUTS_B:-${NUM_ROLLOUTS}}"
# Rollouts at the start of Stage B in which only the critic trains. This is the
# warmup window the incident was reported against, and the window in which the
# value loss is measured.
NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS="${NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS:-${NUM_ROLLOUTS_B}}"

# Episodes per rollout = ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE x N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT; optimizer
# steps per rollout = that, divided by GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE.
ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE="${ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE:-8}"
N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT="${N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT:-2}"
GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE="${GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE:-8}"
LR="${LR:-1e-6}"

# How many leading critic optimizer steps the reported warmup statistics cover.
# Derived rather than guessed, because once Stage B runs past the critic-only
# phase the two are no longer the same thing: averaging the value loss over all
# of a 30-rollout Stage B measures mostly a critic that has already been
# trained, which is not what "warmup value loss" names and not what the
# incident was about.
CRITIC_WARMUP_STEPS=$(( NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS * ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE * N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT / GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE ))
[ "${CRITIC_WARMUP_STEPS}" -gt 0 ] || CRITIC_WARMUP_STEPS=1

# Held-out evaluation during Stage B. 0 disables it, which is what the short
# value-loss-only reproduction wants.
#
# val and test get different sample budgets. val only has to say *when* the
# curve flattens, so 2 samples x 150 tasks is enough; test carries the
# end-to-end claim and is compared per task, where the useful quantity is each
# task's success *rate*, which 1 or 2 samples cannot resolve at all.
EVAL_INTERVAL="${EVAL_INTERVAL:-0}"
N_EVAL_SAMPLES="${N_EVAL_SAMPLES:-2}"
N_EVAL_SAMPLES_TEST="${N_EVAL_SAMPLES_TEST:-4}"

# How often Stage B checkpoints. Trained to convergence, Stage B runs for well
# over an hour, which on a shared host is long enough to be interrupted -- two
# runs of this case were killed from outside the container mid-training, once
# with SIGTERM and once with SIGKILL. So Stage B saves as it goes and a second
# invocation picks up where the first stopped, instead of starting the hour
# again. 0 disables it, which is what the short value-loss-only reproduction
# wants: it writes nothing and measures only the reload.
STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL="${STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL:-0}"

RAY_PORT="${RAY_PORT:-6479}"
DASH_PORT="${DASH_PORT:-8277}"
RAY_TMP="${RAY_TMP:-/tmp/ray_ppo}"

mkdir -p "${OUT_DIR}" "${CKPT_ROOT}" "${ET_SCRATCH}"

# --------------------------------------------------------- 0. the slime source
# The full slime source tree is bundled in the workspace (${SLIME_HOME}) and is
# put ahead of the image's editable install on PYTHONPATH below, so it is the
# copy that trains -- there is nothing to install first.
test -f "${SLIME_HOME}/train.py" || {
    echo "FATAL: bundled slime source not found at ${SLIME_HOME}" >&2
    exit 1
}

# ------------------------------------------------------- 1. the prompt dataset
# prepare.sh ships the already-built dataset (transpiled + validated + split) at
# ${WS}/et_prompts. Seed ET_DATA_ROOT from it so the build below is skipped: the
# 2492->1489 admission is environment-fixed and reproducible, so there is no need
# to re-run the ~40min transpile+validate pass (and ET_SRC is never read). The
# copy lands in a writable, exec-capable dir (ET_DATA_ROOT defaults to /tmp) --
# the bundled tree under /workspace may be a root-owned bind mount. If the
# prebuilt payload is absent, fall through to building from ET_SRC as before.
if [ ! -s "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals.jsonl" ] && [ -s "${WS}/et_prompts/endless_terminals.jsonl" ]; then
    echo "=== seeding ET_DATA_ROOT from prebuilt ${WS}/et_prompts (skipping transpile+validate) ==="
    mkdir -p "${ET_DATA_ROOT}"
    cp -a "${WS}/et_prompts/." "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/"
fi
if [ ! -s "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals.jsonl" ]; then
    echo "=== transpiling + validating the Endless Terminals tasks ==="
    (cd "${WS}" && python3 -m et.build_dataset --src "${ET_SRC}" --out "${ET_DATA_ROOT}") \
        2>&1 | tee "${OUT_DIR}/build_dataset.log"
fi
# Deliberately not silenced. A report that is quietly 0 bytes is worse than one
# that is loudly absent: it reads as "every task was rejected" to anyone who
# opens it later, and that has happened here more than once.
copy_artifact() {   # copy_artifact <src>
    local src="$1" dst="${OUT_DIR}/$(basename "$1")"
    if ! cp -f "${src}" "${dst}"; then
        echo "WARNING: could not copy ${src} into ${OUT_DIR}" >&2
    elif [ ! -s "${dst}" ] && [ -s "${src}" ]; then
        echo "WARNING: ${dst} came out empty although ${src} is not" >&2
    fi
}
copy_artifact "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/validation_report.json"
N_PROMPTS="$(wc -l < "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals.jsonl")"
echo "prompt set: ${N_PROMPTS} validated Endless Terminals tasks"
if [ "${N_PROMPTS}" -lt 4 ]; then
    echo "FATAL: too few tasks survived validation to train on." >&2
    exit 1
fi

# Train on one part of the task set and measure on another. The split is a pure
# function of the admitted list and a fixed seed, so every run trains and is
# scored on exactly the same tasks -- otherwise a comparison between runs is
# partly measuring which tasks each one happened to get.
if [ ! -s "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals_train.jsonl" ]; then
    (cd "${WS}" && python3 -m et.make_splits --prompts "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals.jsonl")
fi
copy_artifact "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/splits.json"
TRAIN_SPLIT="${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals_train.jsonl"
VAL_SPLIT="${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals_val.jsonl"
TEST_SPLIT="${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals_test.jsonl"
printf 'splits: train %s / val %s / test %s\n' \
    "$(wc -l < "${TRAIN_SPLIT}")" "$(wc -l < "${VAL_SPLIT}")" "$(wc -l < "${TEST_SPLIT}")"

# ------------------------------------------------------------- 2. shared args
source "${WS}/configs/model_args.sh"

ROLLOUT_ARGS=(
    --prompt-data "${TRAIN_SPLIT}"
    --input-key prompt
    --label-key label
    --rollout-shuffle
    --rollout-batch-size "${ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE}"
    --n-samples-per-prompt "${N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT}"
    --rollout-max-response-len 2048
    --rollout-temperature 1.0
    --global-batch-size "${GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE}"
    --balance-data
    # The multi-turn terminal loop and its pytest-based episode reward.
    --custom-generate-function-path et.rollout.generate
    --custom-rm-path et.rollout.reward_func
)

PPO_ARGS=(
    --advantage-estimator ppo   # -> args.use_critic
    --gamma 1.0
    --lambd 1.0
    --eps-clip 0.2
    --value-clip 0.2
    --kl-coef 0.0               # no reference model, hence no --ref-load and
    --entropy-coef 0.0          # no HF -> torch_dist conversion step
)

PERF_ARGS=(
    --tensor-model-parallel-size "${TP_SIZE}"
    --pipeline-model-parallel-size 1
    --context-parallel-size 1
    --recompute-granularity full
    --recompute-method uniform
    --recompute-num-layers 1
    --use-dynamic-batch-size
    --max-tokens-per-gpu 8192
)
# Sequence parallelism splits the activations of the non-tensor-parallel ops
# across the TP group, so it is only defined for TP > 1; Megatron asserts on it.
# Spelled as an `if` rather than `[ ... ] && ...`: the latter evaluates to the
# test's status, which under `set -e` ends the script whenever TP_SIZE is 1.
if [ "${TP_SIZE}" -gt 1 ]; then
    PERF_ARGS+=(--sequence-parallel)
fi

OPTIMIZER_ARGS=(
    --optimizer adam
    --lr "${LR}"
    --lr-decay-style constant
    --weight-decay 0.0
    --adam-beta1 0.9
    --adam-beta2 0.95
)

SGLANG_ARGS=(
    --rollout-num-gpus-per-engine "${NUM_GPUS}"
    # Colocated: this fraction is what SGLang keeps, and Megatron's weights,
    # gradients and Adam state have to fit in the rest. At TP 2 each GPU carries
    # half of each role, so 0.55 leaves enough; drop it when NUM_GPUS is 1 and
    # one device has to hold both roles whole.
    --sglang-mem-fraction-static "${SGLANG_MEM_FRACTION}"
)

# Held-out scoring, used only by Stage B. slime evaluates once before the first
# rollout and then every EVAL_INTERVAL rollouts, which gives both the starting
# pass rate and the curve that says whether training has converged.
#
# val and test are evaluated at the same points on purpose. The convergence
# *decision* is read off val; test is reported only at the final point, and
# evaluating it throughout costs generation but no statistical validity, since
# nothing about the run is conditioned on it.
#
# Spelled as an --eval-config YAML rather than --eval-prompt-data because the
# two splits need different sample counts, and --n-samples-per-eval-prompt is
# one global number. Everything the YAML leaves out still falls back to the
# command line (eval_config.py:10 DATASET_RUNTIME_SPECS), so temperature,
# response length and the prompt/label keys are set once, below and above.
EVAL_ARGS=()
if [ "${EVAL_INTERVAL}" -gt 0 ]; then
    cat > "${OUT_DIR}/eval_datasets.yaml" <<YAML
eval:
  datasets:
    - name: et_val
      path: ${VAL_SPLIT}
      n_samples_per_eval_prompt: ${N_EVAL_SAMPLES}
    - name: et_test
      path: ${TEST_SPLIT}
      n_samples_per_eval_prompt: ${N_EVAL_SAMPLES_TEST}
YAML
    EVAL_ARGS=(
        --eval-interval "${EVAL_INTERVAL}"
        --eval-config "${OUT_DIR}/eval_datasets.yaml"
        --eval-max-response-len 2048
        --eval-temperature 1.0
        --log-passrate
        --custom-eval-rollout-log-function-path et.eval_log.log_eval_rollout_data
    )
fi

MISC_ARGS=(
    --attention-dropout 0.0
    --hidden-dropout 0.0
    --accumulate-allreduce-grads-in-fp32
    --attention-softmax-in-fp32
    --attention-backend flash
    --seed 1234
)

# --------------------------------------------------------- 3. per-role configs
# Actor and critic share `args.save` by default, which would make them clobber
# each other's checkpoints (the critic's output layer is [1, hidden_size], the
# actor's is [vocab, hidden_size]), so each role gets its own directory.
cat > "${OUT_DIR}/megatron_roles_stage_a.yaml" <<YAML
# Stage A: "the previous training run". Both roles start from the base model.
megatron:
  - name: stage-a-actor
    role: actor
    overrides:
      load: ${MODEL_DIR}
      save: ${CKPT_ROOT}/actor
  - name: stage-a-critic
    role: critic
    overrides:
      load: ${MODEL_DIR}
      save: ${CKPT_ROOT}/critic
YAML

# Stage B can be entered two ways, and they are not the same event.
#
#   fresh   -- "the model was reloaded". The actor resumes from Stage A's
#              Megatron checkpoint; the critic's backbone comes from the base
#              model.
#
#   resume  -- an interrupted Stage B being continued. Both roles load Stage B's
#              own checkpoints, optimizer state included, and the run continues
#              from the last saved rollout. The first attempt's log is kept,
#              not overwritten (see the STAGE_B_LOG choice below).
STAGE_B_RESUME=0
if [ -f "${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_actor/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt" ] \
   && [ -f "${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_critic/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt" ]; then
    STAGE_B_RESUME=1
fi

if [ "${STAGE_B_RESUME}" = "1" ]; then
    STAGE_B_ACTOR_LOAD="${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_actor"
    STAGE_B_CRITIC_LOAD="${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_critic"
else
    STAGE_B_ACTOR_LOAD="${CKPT_ROOT}/actor"
    STAGE_B_CRITIC_LOAD="${MODEL_DIR}"
fi

cat > "${OUT_DIR}/megatron_roles_stage_b.yaml" <<YAML
# Stage B, $([ "${STAGE_B_RESUME}" = "1" ] && echo "resumed from its own checkpoints" || echo "entered fresh after a reload").
megatron:
  - name: stage-b-actor
    role: actor
    overrides:
      load: ${STAGE_B_ACTOR_LOAD}
      save: ${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_actor
  - name: stage-b-critic
    role: critic
    overrides:
      load: ${STAGE_B_CRITIC_LOAD}
      save: ${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_critic
YAML

# ------------------------------------------------------------------- 4. ray
export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1

ray start --head \
    --node-ip-address 127.0.0.1 \
    --port "${RAY_PORT}" \
    --num-gpus "${NUM_GPUS}" \
    --disable-usage-stats \
    --dashboard-host 127.0.0.1 \
    --dashboard-port "${DASH_PORT}" \
    --temp-dir "${RAY_TMP}"
trap 'ray stop --force >/dev/null 2>&1 || true' EXIT

# `|| true` on the whole pipeline, not decoration: under `pipefail` a `grep`
# that matches nothing fails the pipeline, so on a host with no NVLink -- or in
# a container holding a single GPU, where the topology matrix has no peer links
# to report -- `set -e` would kill the script here. Silently: this sits between
# `ray start` and the first echo of Stage A, so the log just stops.
NVLINK_COUNT="$(nvidia-smi topo -m 2>/dev/null | grep -o 'NV[0-9][0-9]*' | wc -l || true)"
HAS_NVLINK=0
[ "${NVLINK_COUNT:-0}" -gt 0 ] && HAS_NVLINK=1

RUNTIME_ENV_JSON="{
  \"env_vars\": {
    \"PYTHONPATH\": \"/root/Megatron-LM/:${SLIME_HOME}:${WS}\",
    \"CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS\": \"1\",
    \"NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE\": \"${HAS_NVLINK}\",
    \"ET_DATA_ROOT\": \"${ET_DATA_ROOT}\",
    \"ET_EVAL_DUMP_DIR\": \"${OUT_DIR}/eval_episodes\",
    \"ET_SCRATCH\": \"${ET_SCRATCH}\",
    \"ET_MAX_TURNS\": \"${ET_MAX_TURNS}\",
    \"ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS\": \"${ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS}\",
    \"ET_CMD_TIMEOUT\": \"${ET_CMD_TIMEOUT}\",
    \"ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS\": \"${ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS}\"
  }
}"

submit() {   # submit <log-file> <extra args...>
    local log="$1"; shift
    # The entrypoint is an absolute path on purpose: `ray job submit` does not
    # run it in this shell's directory but in the cwd of the Ray head (here
    # /workspace, since no `working_dir` is uploaded), so a bare `train.py`
    # would not be found. Running ${SLIME_HOME}/train.py puts the bundled slime
    # tree on the driver's sys.path[0]; the ray workers get it from ${SLIME_HOME}
    # on PYTHONPATH (RUNTIME_ENV_JSON above), ahead of the image's install.
    ray job submit \
        --address "http://127.0.0.1:${DASH_PORT}" \
        --runtime-env-json "${RUNTIME_ENV_JSON}" \
        -- python3 "${SLIME_HOME}/train.py" \
        --actor-num-nodes 1 \
        --actor-num-gpus-per-node "${NUM_GPUS}" \
        --colocate \
        --hf-checkpoint "${MODEL_DIR}" \
        "${MODEL_ARGS[@]}" \
        "${ROLLOUT_ARGS[@]}" \
        "${PPO_ARGS[@]}" \
        "${PERF_ARGS[@]}" \
        "${OPTIMIZER_ARGS[@]}" \
        "${SGLANG_ARGS[@]}" \
        "${MISC_ARGS[@]}" \
        "$@" 2>&1 | tee "${log}"
}

# Ray forwards actor stdout to the job driver, but keep the raw worker logs too:
# the per-step metrics are emitted by the train actors, not by the driver.
collect_worker_logs() {   # collect_worker_logs <tag>
    # Two statements, not one: `local a=.. b=..` expands every word before it
    # assigns any of them, so referring to ${tag} on the same line would read
    # it while it is still unset -- fatal under `set -u`.
    local tag="$1"
    local dst="${OUT_DIR}/${tag}_worker_logs"
    mkdir -p "${dst}"
    grep -rl "critic-step" "${RAY_TMP}"/session_*/logs/ 2>/dev/null | while read -r f; do
        cp -f "${f}" "${dst}/$(basename "$(dirname "${f}")")_$(basename "${f}")" 2>/dev/null || true
    done
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 5. stage A
echo
echo "############ Stage A: the previous training run ############"
# SKIP_STAGE_A=1 reuses a checkpoint an earlier invocation already wrote, for
# re-running the long Stage B after an interruption. Off by default, and
# refuses to be silently wrong: with no checkpoint there, Stage A runs anyway.
if [ "${SKIP_STAGE_A:-0}" = "1" ] && [ -f "${CKPT_ROOT}/actor/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt" ]; then
    echo "SKIP_STAGE_A=1 and ${CKPT_ROOT}/actor already holds a checkpoint -- reusing it."
else
    submit "${OUT_DIR}/stage_a.log" \
        --megatron-config-path "${OUT_DIR}/megatron_roles_stage_a.yaml" \
        --load "${MODEL_DIR}" \
        --save "${CKPT_ROOT}/actor" \
        --save-interval 1 \
        --num-rollout "${NUM_ROLLOUTS}" \
        --num-critic-only-steps 0
    collect_worker_logs stage_a
fi

echo
echo "checkpoint written by Stage A:"
ls -1 "${CKPT_ROOT}/actor" 2>/dev/null || true
test -f "${CKPT_ROOT}/actor/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt" || {
    echo "FATAL: Stage A did not produce a resumable Megatron checkpoint." >&2
    exit 1
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 6. stage B
echo
echo "############ Stage B: reload, then critic warmup ############"
# --save-interval has to be set because --save is: Megatron's validate_args
# asserts the two go together. With STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL=0 it is set far
# larger than the number of rollouts Stage B takes, so Stage B measures the
# reload and writes nothing -- the only checkpoint the short reproduction needs
# is the one Stage A already produced.
#
# --override-opt-param-scheduler is what lets Stage B be longer than Stage A.
# slime derives `train_iters` from --num-rollout (model.py:203) and Megatron
# stores the resulting LR/weight-decay horizons in the checkpoint, then asserts
# on reload that the new arguments imply the same ones ("total number of
# iterations do not match"). The flag says "use the command line, not the
# checkpoint", which is exactly right here: Stage B is a new training run that
# happens to start from Stage A's weights, not a resumption of Stage A.
STAGE_B_ARGS=(
    --megatron-config-path "${OUT_DIR}/megatron_roles_stage_b.yaml"
    --load "${STAGE_B_ACTOR_LOAD}"
    --save "${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_actor"
    --save-interval "$([ "${STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL}" -gt 0 ] && echo "${STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL}" || echo 1000)"
    --override-opt-param-scheduler
    --num-rollout "${NUM_ROLLOUTS_B}"
    --num-critic-only-steps "${NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS}"
)

STAGE_B_LOG="${OUT_DIR}/stage_b.log"
if [ "${STAGE_B_RESUME}" = "1" ]; then
    # The first attempt's log holds the warmup window that the value-loss
    # verdict is read from, so a resume must not overwrite it.
    n=1
    while [ -e "${OUT_DIR}/stage_b_resume_${n}.log" ]; do n=$((n + 1)); done
    STAGE_B_LOG="${OUT_DIR}/stage_b_resume_${n}.log"
    echo "resuming Stage B from ${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_{actor,critic}" \
         "(iteration $(cat "${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_critic/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt")); log -> ${STAGE_B_LOG}"
    # --start-rollout-id is deliberately NOT passed here. slime takes the start
    # id from the *critic*'s loaded checkpoint when a critic is in play
    # (placement_group.py:212), and Stage B saves at `iteration = rollout_id`,
    # so omitting it resumes at exactly the rollout after the last saved one.
else
    # --start-rollout-id 0 pins the warmup window: without it the start id is
    # inferred from whichever checkpoint the critic loaded, and on a fresh
    # Stage B the critic loads a plain HF directory (iteration 0).
    STAGE_B_ARGS+=(--start-rollout-id 0)
fi

submit "${STAGE_B_LOG}" "${STAGE_B_ARGS[@]}" "${EVAL_ARGS[@]+"${EVAL_ARGS[@]}"}"
collect_worker_logs stage_b

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 7. verdict
echo
echo "############ critic warmup value loss ############"
python3 "${WS}/tools/parse_value_loss.py" \
    "${OUT_DIR}/stage_b.log" \
    --warmup-steps "${CRITIC_WARMUP_STEPS}" \
    --out "${OUT_DIR}/stage_b_value_loss.json"

python3 "${WS}/tools/parse_value_loss.py" \
    "${OUT_DIR}/stage_a.log" \
    --out "${OUT_DIR}/stage_a_value_loss.json" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

echo
echo "artifacts in ${OUT_DIR}:"
ls -1 "${OUT_DIR}"

240	    # gradients and Adam state have to fit in the rest. At TP 2 each GPU carries
241	    # half of each role, so 0.55 leaves enough; drop it when NUM_GPUS is 1 and
242	    # one device has to hold both roles whole.
243	    --sglang-mem-fraction-static "${SGLANG_MEM_FRACTION}"
244	)
245	
246	# Held-out scoring, used only by Stage B. slime evaluates once before the first
247	# rollout and then every EVAL_INTERVAL rollouts, which gives both the starting
248	# pass rate and the curve that says whether training has converged.
249	#
250	# val and test are evaluated at the same points on purpose. The convergence
251	# *decision* is read off val; test is reported only at the final point, and
252	# evaluating it throughout costs generation but no statistical validity, since
253	# nothing about the run is conditioned on it.
254	#
255	# Spelled as an --eval-config YAML rather than --eval-prompt-data because the
256	# two splits need different sample counts, and --n-samples-per-eval-prompt is
257	# one global number. Everything the YAML leaves out still falls back to the
258	# command line (eval_config.py:10 DATASET_RUNTIME_SPECS), so temperature,
259	# response length and the prompt/label keys are set once, below and above.
260	EVAL_ARGS=()
261	if [ "${EVAL_INTERVAL}" -gt 0 ]; then
262	    cat > "${OUT_DIR}/eval_datasets.yaml" <<YAML
263	eval:
264	  datasets:
265	    - name: et_val
266	      path: ${VAL_SPLIT}
267	      n_samples_per_eval_prompt: ${N_EVAL_SAMPLES}
268	    - name: et_test
269	      path: ${TEST_SPLIT}
270	      n_samples_per_eval_prompt: ${N_EVAL_SAMPLES_TEST}
271	YAML
272	    EVAL_ARGS=(
273	        --eval-interval "${EVAL_INTERVAL}"
274	        --eval-config "${OUT_DIR}/eval_datasets.yaml"
275	        --eval-max-response-len 2048
276	        --eval-temperature 1.0
277	        --log-passrate
278	        --custom-eval-rollout-log-function-path et.eval_log.log_eval_rollout_data
279	    )
280	fi
281	
282	MISC_ARGS=(
283	    --attention-dropout 0.0
284	    --hidden-dropout 0.0
285	    --accumulate-allreduce-grads-in-fp32
286	    --attention-softmax-in-fp32
287	    --attention-backend flash
288	    --seed 1234
289	)
290	
291	# --------------------------------------------------------- 3. per-role configs
292	# Actor and critic share `args.save` by default, which would make them clobber
293	# each other's checkpoints (the critic's output layer is [1, hidden_size], the
294	# actor's is [vocab, hidden_size]), so each role gets its own directory.
295	cat > "${OUT_DIR}/megatron_roles_stage_a.yaml" <<YAML
296	# Stage A: "the previous training run". Both roles start from the base model.
297	megatron:
298	  - name: stage-a-actor
299	    role: actor
300	    overrides:
301	      load: ${MODEL_DIR}
302	      save: ${CKPT_ROOT}/actor
303	  - name: stage-a-critic
304	    role: critic
305	    overrides:
306	      load: ${MODEL_DIR}
307	      save: ${CKPT_ROOT}/critic
308	YAML
309	
310	# Stage B can be entered two ways, and they are not the same event.
311	#
312	#   fresh   -- "the model was reloaded". The actor resumes from Stage A's
313	#              Megatron checkpoint; the critic's backbone comes from the base
314	#              model.
315	#
316	#   resume  -- an interrupted Stage B being continued. Both roles load Stage B's
317	#              own checkpoints, optimizer state included, and the run continues
318	#              from the last saved rollout. The first attempt's log is kept,
319	#              not overwritten (see the STAGE_B_LOG choice below).
320	STAGE_B_RESUME=0
321	if [ -f "${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_actor/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt" ] \
322	   && [ -f "${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_critic/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt" ]; then
323	    STAGE_B_RESUME=1
324	fi
325	
326	if [ "${STAGE_B_RESUME}" = "1" ]; then
327	    STAGE_B_ACTOR_LOAD="${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_actor"
328	    STAGE_B_CRITIC_LOAD="${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_critic"
329	else
330	    STAGE_B_ACTOR_LOAD="${CKPT_ROOT}/actor"
331	    STAGE_B_CRITIC_LOAD="${MODEL_DIR}"
332	fi
333	
334	cat > "${OUT_DIR}/megatron_roles_stage_b.yaml" <<YAML
335	# Stage B, $([ "${STAGE_B_RESUME}" = "1" ] && echo "resumed from its own checkpoints" || echo "entered fresh after a reload").
336	megatron:
337	  - name: stage-b-actor
338	    role: actor
339	    overrides:
340	      load: ${STAGE_B_ACTOR_LOAD}
341	      save: ${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_actor
342	  - name: stage-b-critic
343	    role: critic
344	    overrides:
345	      load: ${STAGE_B_CRITIC_LOAD}
346	      save: ${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_critic
347	YAML
348	
349	# ------------------------------------------------------------------- 4. ray
350	export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
351	
352	ray start --head \
353	    --node-ip-address 127.0.0.1 \
354	    --port "${RAY_PORT}" \
355	    --num-gpus "${NUM_GPUS}" \
356	    --disable-usage-stats \
357	    --dashboard-host 127.0.0.1 \
358	    --dashboard-port "${DASH_PORT}" \
359	    --temp-dir "${RAY_TMP}"
360	trap 'ray stop --force >/dev/null 2>&1 || true' EXIT
361	
362	# `|| true` on the whole pipeline, not decoration: under `pipefail` a `grep`
363	# that matches nothing fails the pipeline, so on a host with no NVLink -- or in
364	# a container holding a single GPU, where the topology matrix has no peer links
365	# to report -- `set -e` would kill the script here. Silently: this sits between
366	# `ray start` and the first echo of Stage A, so the log just stops.
367	NVLINK_COUNT="$(nvidia-smi topo -m 2>/dev/null | grep -o 'NV[0-9][0-9]*' | wc -l || true)"
368	HAS_NVLINK=0
369	[ "${NVLINK_COUNT:-0}" -gt 0 ] && HAS_NVLINK=1
370	
371	RUNTIME_ENV_JSON="{
372	  \"env_vars\": {
373	    \"PYTHONPATH\": \"/root/Megatron-LM/:${SLIME_HOME}:${WS}\",
374	    \"CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS\": \"1\",
375	    \"NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE\": \"${HAS_NVLINK}\",
376	    \"ET_DATA_ROOT\": \"${ET_DATA_ROOT}\",
377	    \"ET_EVAL_DUMP_DIR\": \"${OUT_DIR}/eval_episodes\",
378	    \"ET_SCRATCH\": \"${ET_SCRATCH}\",
379	    \"ET_MAX_TURNS\": \"${ET_MAX_TURNS}\",
380	    \"ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS\": \"${ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS}\",
381	    \"ET_CMD_TIMEOUT\": \"${ET_CMD_TIMEOUT}\",
382	    \"ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS\": \"${ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS}\"
383	  }
384	}"
385	
386	submit() {   # submit <log-file> <extra args...>
387	    local log="$1"; shift
388	    # The entrypoint is an absolute path on purpose: `ray job submit` does not
389	    # run it in this shell's directory but in the cwd of the Ray head (here
390	    # /workspace, since no `working_dir` is uploaded), so a bare `train.py`
391	    # would not be found. Running ${SLIME_HOME}/train.py puts the bundled slime
392	    # tree on the driver's sys.path[0]; the ray workers get it from ${SLIME_HOME}
393	    # on PYTHONPATH (RUNTIME_ENV_JSON above), ahead of the image's install.
394	    ray job submit \
395	        --address "http://127.0.0.1:${DASH_PORT}" \
396	        --runtime-env-json "${RUNTIME_ENV_JSON}" \
397	        -- python3 "${SLIME_HOME}/train.py" \
398	        --actor-num-nodes 1 \
399	        --actor-num-gpus-per-node "${NUM_GPUS}" \
400	        --colocate \
401	        --hf-checkpoint "${MODEL_DIR}" \
402	        "${MODEL_ARGS[@]}" \
403	        "${ROLLOUT_ARGS[@]}" \
404	        "${PPO_ARGS[@]}" \
405	        "${PERF_ARGS[@]}" \
406	        "${OPTIMIZER_ARGS[@]}" \
407	        "${SGLANG_ARGS[@]}" \
408	        "${MISC_ARGS[@]}" \
409	        "$@" 2>&1 | tee "${log}"
410	}
411	
412	# Ray forwards actor stdout to the job driver, but keep the raw worker logs too:
413	# the per-step metrics are emitted by the train actors, not by the driver.
414	collect_worker_logs() {   # collect_worker_logs <tag>
415	    # Two statements, not one: `local a=.. b=..` expands every word before it
416	    # assigns any of them, so referring to ${tag} on the same line would read
417	    # it while it is still unset -- fatal under `set -u`.
418	    local tag="$1"
419	    local dst="${OUT_DIR}/${tag}_worker_logs"
420	    mkdir -p "${dst}"
421	    grep -rl "critic-step" "${RAY_TMP}"/session_*/logs/ 2>/dev/null | while read -r f; do
422	        cp -f "${f}" "${dst}/$(basename "$(dirname "${f}")")_$(basename "${f}")" 2>/dev/null || true
423	    done
424	}
425	
426	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 5. stage A
427	echo
428	echo "############ Stage A: the previous training run ############"
429	# SKIP_STAGE_A=1 reuses a checkpoint an earlier invocation already wrote, for
430	# re-running the long Stage B after an interruption. Off by default, and
431	# refuses to be silently wrong: with no checkpoint there, Stage A runs anyway.
432	if [ "${SKIP_STAGE_A:-0}" = "1" ] && [ -f "${CKPT_ROOT}/actor/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt" ]; then
433	    echo "SKIP_STAGE_A=1 and ${CKPT_ROOT}/actor already holds a checkpoint -- reusing it."
434	else
435	    submit "${OUT_DIR}/stage_a.log" \
436	        --megatron-config-path "${OUT_DIR}/megatron_roles_stage_a.yaml" \
437	        --load "${MODEL_DIR}" \
438	        --save "${CKPT_ROOT}/actor" \
439	        --save-interval 1 \
440	        --num-rollout "${NUM_ROLLOUTS}" \
441	        --num-critic-only-steps 0
442	    collect_worker_logs stage_a
443	fi
444	
445	echo
446	echo "checkpoint written by Stage A:"
447	ls -1 "${CKPT_ROOT}/actor" 2>/dev/null || true
448	test -f "${CKPT_ROOT}/actor/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt" || {
449	    echo "FATAL: Stage A did not produce a resumable Megatron checkpoint." >&2
450	    exit 1
451	}
452	
453	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 6. stage B
454	echo
455	echo "############ Stage B: reload, then critic warmup ############"
456	# --save-interval has to be set because --save is: Megatron's validate_args
457	# asserts the two go together. With STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL=0 it is set far
458	# larger than the number of rollouts Stage B takes, so Stage B measures the
459	# reload and writes nothing -- the only checkpoint the short reproduction needs
460	# is the one Stage A already produced.
461	#
462	# --override-opt-param-scheduler is what lets Stage B be longer than Stage A.
463	# slime derives `train_iters` from --num-rollout (model.py:203) and Megatron
464	# stores the resulting LR/weight-decay horizons in the checkpoint, then asserts
465	# on reload that the new arguments imply the same ones ("total number of
466	# iterations do not match"). The flag says "use the command line, not the
467	# checkpoint", which is exactly right here: Stage B is a new training run that
468	# happens to start from Stage A's weights, not a resumption of Stage A.
469	STAGE_B_ARGS=(
470	    --megatron-config-path "${OUT_DIR}/megatron_roles_stage_b.yaml"
471	    --load "${STAGE_B_ACTOR_LOAD}"
472	    --save "${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_actor"
473	    --save-interval "$([ "${STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL}" -gt 0 ] && echo "${STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL}" || echo 1000)"
474	    --override-opt-param-scheduler
475	    --num-rollout "${NUM_ROLLOUTS_B}"
476	    --num-critic-only-steps "${NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS}"
477	)
478	
479	STAGE_B_LOG="${OUT_DIR}/stage_b.log"
480	if [ "${STAGE_B_RESUME}" = "1" ]; then
481	    # The first attempt's log holds the warmup window that the value-loss
482	    # verdict is read from, so a resume must not overwrite it.
483	    n=1
484	    while [ -e "${OUT_DIR}/stage_b_resume_${n}.log" ]; do n=$((n + 1)); done
485	    STAGE_B_LOG="${OUT_DIR}/stage_b_resume_${n}.log"
486	    echo "resuming Stage B from ${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_{actor,critic}" \
487	         "(iteration $(cat "${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_critic/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt")); log -> ${STAGE_B_LOG}"
488	    # --start-rollout-id is deliberately NOT passed here. slime takes the start
489	    # id from the *critic*'s loaded checkpoint when a critic is in play
490	    # (placement_group.py:212), and Stage B saves at `iteration = rollout_id`,
491	    # so omitting it resumes at exactly the rollout after the last saved one.
492	else
493	    # --start-rollout-id 0 pins the warmup window: without it the start id is
494	    # inferred from whichever checkpoint the critic loaded, and on a fresh
495	    # Stage B the critic loads a plain HF directory (iteration 0).
496	    STAGE_B_ARGS+=(--start-rollout-id 0)
497	fi
498	
499	submit "${STAGE_B_LOG}" "${STAGE_B_ARGS[@]}" "${EVAL_ARGS[@]+"${EVAL_ARGS[@]}"}"
500	collect_worker_logs stage_b
501	
502	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 7. verdict
503	echo
504	echo "############ critic warmup value loss ############"
505	python3 "${WS}/tools/parse_value_loss.py" \
506	    "${OUT_DIR}/stage_b.log" \
507	    --warmup-steps "${CRITIC_WARMUP_STEPS}" \
508	    --out "${OUT_DIR}/stage_b_value_loss.json"
509	
510	python3 "${WS}/tools/parse_value_loss.py" \
511	    "${OUT_DIR}/stage_a.log" \
512	    --out "${OUT_DIR}/stage_a_value_loss.json" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
513	
514	echo
515	echo "artifacts in ${OUT_DIR}:"
516	ls -1 "${OUT_DIR}"
517

1	"""Multi-turn Endless Terminals rollout for slime.
2	
3	Wired in via:
4	    --custom-generate-function-path et.rollout.generate
5	    --custom-rm-path                et.rollout.reward_func
6	
7	One sample == one terminal episode. Each turn the policy emits exactly one
8	`<command>...</command>` (or `<action>done</action>`); the command runs in the
9	episode's private shell and the harness-formatted result is appended to the
10	context as a non-trainable user turn. The episode reward is the task's own
11	pytest verifier: 1.0 or 0.0, awarded once at the end of the episode.
12	
13	The system prompt below is copied verbatim from the Endless Terminals reference
14	transcripts (`solution/o3_summary.json`), as is the observation wording, so the
15	policy sees the same interface the dataset was built against.
16	"""
17	
18	from __future__ import annotations
19	
20	import asyncio
21	import logging
22	import os
23	import re
24	
25	from slime.rollout.sglang_rollout import GenerateState
26	from slime.utils.http_utils import post
27	from slime.utils.types import Sample
28	
29	from et.sandbox import Episode, check_exec_capable
30	
31	SYSTEM_PROMPT = """You are a highly capable Linux terminal agent operating strictly via a single-shell-command interface.
32	Goal: complete the user's task.
33	
34	Rules:
35	- Output exactly one of the following per turn:
36	  1) <command>THE_SINGLE_SHELL_COMMAND</command>
37	  OR
38	  2) <action>done</action>
39	- Don't use interactive commands and confirmations; use non-interactive flags.
40	- Prefer simple, robust CLI tools; write files explicitly when needed.
41	- If you believe the task is solved, emit <action>done</action>.
42	- Hint: you might want to run commands interactively to see the output and then write the command. Don't just pipe the commands.
43	- Only your first command in command tags will be executed. So don't respond with multiple commands.
44	- Hint: Verify your solution once you are done. Eg: you can use cat to see the input and the output.
45	- Do not just write long bash scripts. Write the commands that you would write in a terminal."""
46	
47	DATA_ROOT = os.environ.get("ET_DATA_ROOT", "/tmp/et_prompts")
48	# Must allow execution, so not under /dev/shm -- see et.sandbox.check_exec_capable.
49	SCRATCH_ROOT = os.environ.get("ET_SCRATCH", "/tmp/et_episodes")
50	MAX_TURNS = int(os.environ.get("ET_MAX_TURNS", "8"))
51	MAX_NEW_TOKENS_PER_TURN = int(os.environ.get("ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS", "512"))
52	CMD_TIMEOUT = float(os.environ.get("ET_CMD_TIMEOUT", "20"))
53	MAX_OBS_CHARS = int(os.environ.get("ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS", "1500"))
54	# Hard ceiling on one episode, covering everything: generation, the shell, the
55	# verifier and teardown. Every individual step is already bounded, yet the run
56	# still hung -- slime builds its HTTP client with `httpx.Timeout(None)`, so a
57	# `/generate` that never comes back waits forever, and asyncio's
58	# `Process.wait()` has its own way of never resolving (see sandbox.REAP_TIMEOUT).
59	# Both drivers await every episode before returning, so one episode that never
60	# finishes stalls the entire rollout rather than failing it. The default is
61	# deliberately far above any legitimate episode -- 6 turns of generation plus
62	# 6x20s of commands plus a 180s verifier -- so this only ever fires on a hang.
63	EPISODE_TIMEOUT = float(os.environ.get("ET_EPISODE_TIMEOUT", "900"))
64	
65	STOP_STRINGS = ["</command>", "</action>"]
66	_OBS_SENTINEL = "@@ET_OBSERVATION@@"
67	
68	_COMMAND_RE = re.compile(r"<command>(.*?)(?:</command>|\Z)", re.DOTALL)
69	_ACTION_RE = re.compile(r"<action>\s*done\s*</action>", re.IGNORECASE)
70	
71	
72	class _Chat:
73	    """Derives the chat-template glue once, without hardcoding ChatML.
74	
75	    `head` is the token prefix the policy generates from. `tail` is the text
76	    that must follow a generated assistant turn in order to inject one user
77	    turn and re-open the assistant turn.
78	    """
79	
80	    def __init__(self, tokenizer) -> None:
81	        kwargs = {"tokenize": False, "add_generation_prompt": True, "enable_thinking": False}
82	        probe_msgs = [{"role": "system", "content": "S"}, {"role": "user", "content": "U"}]
83	        head = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(probe_msgs, **kwargs)
84	        full = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
85	            probe_msgs
86	            + [{"role": "assistant", "content": "A"}, {"role": "user", "content": _OBS_SENTINEL}],
87	            **kwargs,
88	        )
89	        prefix = os.path.commonprefix([head, full])
90	        assert full[len(prefix) : len(prefix) + 1] == "A", "unexpected chat template shape"
91	        self._tail = full[len(prefix) + 1 :]
92	        assert _OBS_SENTINEL in self._tail, "could not locate the observation slot in the chat template"
93	        self._kwargs = kwargs
94	
95	    def prompt(self, tokenizer, instruction: str) -> str:
96	        return tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
97	            [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT}, {"role": "user", "content": instruction}],
98	            **self._kwargs,
99	        )
100	
101	    def observation(self, text: str) -> str:
102	        return self._tail.replace(_OBS_SENTINEL, text)
103	
104	
105	_CHAT: _Chat | None = None
106	_SCRATCH_CHECKED = False
107	
108	
109	def _chat(tokenizer) -> _Chat:
110	    global _CHAT
111	    if _CHAT is None:
112	        _CHAT = _Chat(tokenizer)
113	    return _CHAT
114	
115	
116	def _check_scratch_once() -> None:
117	    global _SCRATCH_CHECKED
118	    if not _SCRATCH_CHECKED:
119	        check_exec_capable(SCRATCH_ROOT)
120	        _SCRATCH_CHECKED = True
121	
122	
123	def parse_action(text: str) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
124	    """Return ("command", cmd) / ("done", None) / ("invalid", None).
125	
126	    Mirrors the harness rule "only your first command in command tags will be
127	    executed": whichever of `<command>` / `<action>` appears first wins.
128	    """
129	    cmd_match = _COMMAND_RE.search(text)
130	    act_match = _ACTION_RE.search(text)
131	    if act_match and (cmd_match is None or act_match.start() < cmd_match.start()):
132	        return "done", None
133	    if cmd_match:
134	        cmd = cmd_match.group(1).strip()
135	        return ("command", cmd) if cmd else ("invalid", None)
136	    return "invalid", None
137	
138	
139	def _abort(args, sample: Sample, turns: int, **extra) -> Sample:
140	    """Finish a sample that is giving up, with every field slime will index.
